Please read /papers/investigations-6/notes/01_BRANCH_OVERVIEWS_AND_CONTINUATION_20261113.md, and engage in the research there. 

Track your progress in the research progress folder, write research notes in the notes folder, and record chat history in the chat-histories folder. Please provide guidance for the continuation at the end of your research, and a continuation note for model changes, also mentioning the suggested continuation model in the chat.

I’ll read the branch overview and the project’s established results, then work on a concrete next step. I’ll save the research, progress record, and handoff guidance in investigations-6 and set up this chat’s history capture.

The continuation calls for four parallel branches, with Astra/Ultra selecting the questions and Sol 6.1/Ultra carrying out the fixed derivations. Three branch workers are now reading their source material. I’m checking the infinite-product branch and shared interfaces, and the local history source is available for this chat.

Two promising directions are emerging: a finite-chain error bound for evaluating the field, and a coefficient bound that could make that error estimate explicit. The infinite-product branch is also testing whether exact integration within each source cell avoids the aliasing caused by replacing cells with point masses. These are approximation results, not claims about the zeros.

The coefficient branch has found a concrete candidate bound,
\(\beta_n+\beta_{n+1}\le[\operatorname{arcosh}(2n+12)/4]^2\).
If the derivation checks out, it will supply an explicit input to the chain error bound without assuming an unknown coefficient asymptotic. I’m keeping it marked as a target until the execution and assessment are complete.

The first execution requests are being saved with fixed inputs, domains, and acceptance tests. The most useful shared direction is now clear: combine the coefficient estimate with the finite-chain error formula to obtain a depth-versus-accuracy bound for the actual field. That would add a quantitative result beyond the inherited representation identities.

The QTT question is now fixed: prove an error allowance on a specified height box and compare it with direct integration of the same polynomial. The packet explicitly separates formal low-rank representation from the cost of constructing its coefficients. It also records that the scalar baseline avoids the QTT quadrature error, so a successful bound alone will not establish a computational advantage.

The coefficient derivation has passed its first execution check. The shared plan now points to a depth bound of order \(K\log K\), where \(K\) combines the height range and requested accuracy. The remaining checks are the finite-chain proof and the composition of the two results, including their constants and normalization.

The finite-chain derivation also checks out: it bounds the literal scalar field error while retaining the omitted boundary coupling and the factor \(1/2\). It does not bound the whole wavefunction. Separate assessment passes are now checking the branch proofs before I record the shared depth result and continuation guidance.

The exact-cell construction has passed its constant checks too: its total allowance is below \(5\times10^{-7}\) for every real height and \(|\operatorname{Im}z|\le8\), with the stated cutoff and refinement. This is an absolute-error theorem using exact cell masses. Computing those masses efficiently, and obtaining relative accuracy near zeros, remain separate questions.

The coefficient and chain results are now saved as proofs, and the shared transfer request is pinned to those files. The final guidance will distinguish what has been obtained—explicit approximation bounds—from the remaining practical work: coefficient acquisition, arithmetic precision, relative accuracy, and any signed-field application.

The shared calculation checks out: with \(K=X+\log(1/\varepsilon)+1\), the sufficient depth \(N=\lceil4K\log(16K)\rceil\) bounds scalar error by \(H_{1/2}(0)\varepsilon\) on the chosen real-height interval. The QTT bound also passes its original test. I’m finishing the assessments and writing the handoff around the next practical gap: acquiring the finite coefficients with controlled error.

The shared result and its assessment are saved. A second worker also checked the transfer constants and the summary’s scope without finding a mathematical error. The QTT proof and assessment are the last artifacts being finalized; I’m then checking the saved links and records and arranging capture of this turn’s final reply.

All four branches and the shared transfer are complete within their declared scopes, with internal assessments saved. The roundup and model-change handoff are in place. The record check found no unexplained input changes, broken links, or oversized files. I recommend Astra/Ultra next to select the coefficient-acquisition method, then Sol 6.1/Ultra for the fixed execution.

Completed the first bounded research round across all four branches, including internal assessments.

The main result is an explicit sufficient chain depth:
\[
N=\lceil4K\log(16K)\rceil,\qquad K=X+\log(1/\varepsilon)+1,
\]
giving scalar error at most \(H_{1/2}(0)\varepsilon\) on the prescribed real-height interval. The round also established a coefficient envelope, a formal QTT rank/error bound, and a uniform exact-cell approximation bound.

These remain approximation results, without a zero-exclusion or computational-speed claim.

Saved:

- [Research results and limitations](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/notes/04_FIRST_RESEARCH_ROUND_RESULTS_20261114.md)
- [Progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/research-progress/01_TENSOR_NETWORK_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_20261113.md)
- [Continuation and model-change handoff](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/notes/05_RESEARCH_CONTINUATION_AND_MODEL_HANDOFF_20261114.md)

**Next: [B] TN6-B02 — GPT-6 Astra / Ultra**, to select a certified coefficient-acquisition method and matched finite benchmark. Use **GPT-6.1 Sol / Ultra** for the resulting fixed execution.

Chat history is registered and refreshed; capture of this final reply is queued.
Please continue with TN6-B02 using Astra Ultra, then use Sol 6.1 Ultra for ready execution tasks. Keep updating the research notes, progress register, chat history, and continuation guidance.

I’ll continue TN6-B02 with Astra/Ultra, then pass any fixed execution task to Sol 6.1/Ultra. I’ll first check the saved handoff and refresh this chat’s history, then keep the notes and progress register current through the next bounded research round.

TN6-B02 is now active. The decision is how to turn the analytical chain bound into a small certified calculation: acquire the coefficients, carry their uncertainty through the field evaluation, and compare against the same field computed directly. I’m checking existing interval-arithmetic routines so the execution can reuse established source and tail handling.

The available runtime supports rigorous integration and matrix arithmetic. Astra is narrowing the benchmark to a 16-site chain on \(|x|\le8\), using interval-enclosed moments and direct source integration as the comparison. This will test whether coefficient acquisition and conditioning can support the requested error bound; the result will not depend on a presumed tensor speedup.

The benchmark is now specified: moments through degree 32, a 16-site chain, and a \(10^{-8}\) error target measured against the fixed positive base mass. The execution will separate the uniform analytical allowance from nine computed readouts, use exact outward interval endpoints in its record, and stay within fixed precision and runtime limits.

The selected error calculation includes a useful stability bound: uncertainty in the Jacobi matrix contributes at most \(9\delta\) on this domain, where \(\delta\) bounds the matrix error. Sol will now need to establish the actual moment, coefficient, mass, and evaluation errors. A separate Sol worker will assess the completed certificate.

Sol has verified the frozen inputs and the complete-source tail formulas. The implementation is now adding runtime limits and saving progress after each stage, so a failed attempt will leave a reviewable record. The main numerical question is how much precision the moment matrices need to yield positive, narrow coefficient intervals.

The numerical work is still in implementation; no coefficient certificate has been claimed yet. The saved plan fixes how to handle a failed pivot, an overly wide interval, or an exhausted work limit. A failed test will remain a result for this specific method and benchmark, rather than trigger an unrecorded larger run.

TN6-B02 is complete. Sol 6.1 Ultra is implementing its fixed coefficient-acquisition test. Once the run returns, a separate Sol 6.1 Ultra assessment will check the certificate before I update the conclusions and continuation guidance.

The calculation passed at 256-bit precision. At 128 bits, the coefficient intervals were too wide for the fixed error budget; that failed attempt is preserved. The successful attempt certified all sixteen couplings and all nine matched readouts. I’m now checking the saved evidence and the scope of that result.

The certified error is much smaller than the requested tolerance on this finite domain. The cost result needs more restraint: acquisition plus nine chain evaluations took longer than the nine direct integrals in this run. Both methods exceeded the accuracy target, so this establishes a usable finite calculation without establishing a speed advantage.

The separate assessment is underway, including one replay of the unchanged calculation. I’m also preparing the handoff and preserving the exact inputs used by the certificate, so updated research summaries will not prevent a later replay.

The assessment replay passed without changing the calculation. The remaining checks are the exact error calculations, the preserved 128-bit failure, and the wording of the conclusions. The continuation note proposes Astra Ultra for the next decision: choose a worthwhile reuse or harder-domain benchmark, or stop this computational direction.

The assessment accepted the result as a finite certificate at the issued scope, with no correction requested. The replay matched the scientific values, decisions, and counts. I’m finishing the records with the scope intact: certified absolute approximation on this domain, no zero-exclusion result, and no demonstrated speed advantage.

The research summary and continuation note are saved. The replay check also passed after the summary update: it restores the exact historical guidance and verifies all original inputs. The certificate, generator, and failed precision attempt remain unchanged.

All mathematical and numerical checks are complete. A final document check found damaged formula formatting in the assessment; that is being repaired before the record is closed. The result and certificate are unchanged.

Completed TN6-B02 with Astra Ultra, followed by TN6-E02 and its separate internal assessment with Sol 6.1 Ultra.

The 256-bit calculation certified sixteen couplings and nine readouts. Uniform ideal error is below \(1.515\times10^{-25}H_{1/2}(0)\) for \(|x|\le8,\ 0\le\tau\le1/2\). The failed 128-bit attempt is preserved. Direct integration was faster on this benchmark.

[Research results](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/notes/07_TN6_FINITE_ACQUISITION_ROUND_RESULTS_20261114.md), the progress register, and chat history are updated; final-message capture is queued.

**Suggested continuation model: Astra Ultra** to select a worthwhile next benchmark, then **Sol 6.1 Ultra** for ready execution. The [continuation and model-change note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/notes/08_TN6_CONTINUATION_AND_MODEL_HANDOFF_20261114.md) gives the bounded next steps.

Please write draft manuscripts for all of the sub-investigations. Please focus on analytical results, leaving any numerics for supporting evidence. Please develop the ideas systematically, and methodically derive all of the relevant results, maximizing the coherence of the development of ideas, and the elegance of the results. At the end, describe the outstanding challenges. Please follow the LARGE_FILES guidance and do not save the PDF within the repository.

I’ll develop a manuscript for each of the four sub-investigations, building the exposition around the analytical results and their proofs. I’ll keep numerics as supporting evidence, state the outstanding challenges, and place compiled PDFs outside the repository.

The four drafts will use a common source normalization and notation. Each will develop its own argument from definitions through proofs, with the shared coefficient-to-chain result connecting the papers. The existing certificate will appear as supporting evidence in the Jacobi-chain draft.

The proofs make two distinctions that the drafts will emphasize. Coefficient bounds give scalar-approximation estimates, but do not by themselves control the full evolving state or exclude zeros. Similarly, convergence of the dyadic states does not automatically establish convergence of an infinite product of operators.

The QTT draft is written and compiles. It derives the polynomial tensor cores, the heat generator, the fixed-box error bound, and the comparison with direct polynomial integration. Its final section identifies what remains to turn the formal construction into a practical method.

The QTT, Jacobi-chain, and dyadic-product drafts now compile. Their analytical checks are consistent so far. The Volterra draft is in progress, developing the recurrence and time evolution before deriving the coefficient bounds. All reading PDFs are being kept outside the repository.

The cross-check has found one omission in the Volterra draft: it needs the explicit normalization connecting its kernel to the completed zeta function. I’m adding that derivation, then finishing the PDF checks and updating the research records and continuation guidance.

Each draft now follows a proof-led sequence from the common theta source to its branch’s quantitative results. The closing sections identify what remains open: sharper coefficient estimates, control as height grows, certified input costs, and a source-specific signed estimate. I’m giving those analytical questions priority in the continuation guidance.

All four PDFs compile without warnings, and the internal cross-review accepts the drafts within their stated scope. I’m checking the final page layouts and preserving the source versions and summary changes so earlier certificates remain reproducible.

The four manuscripts total 31 pages. The final layouts are checked, and the frozen inputs for the earlier finite-chain certificate still reconstruct exactly. I’m finishing the navigation and integrity checks; the continuation note recommends Astra Ultra for the next analytical choice, then Sol 6.1 Ultra for a fixed execution task.
